design_decisions: The new error owns Vec<u8> and PatchError with no borrowed lifetimes. It implements Debug, Display and Error, exposes the typed PatchError through source(), and provides error() and into_parts(). PatchError gained an additive Error implementation; its variants and existing public data types/signatures remain unchanged.

Both entrypoints share plan_chart_edits and splice validation. Range validation precedes sorted overlap validation, preserving existing rejection ordering. Final output size is checked before mutation with existing range-error variants.

The owned executor first compacts untouched bytes in the original vector, truncates to that compacted length, resizes to the final length, and places fragments and retained gaps backward. This requires no full input clone or second full output buffer and avoids temporary growth beyond the final length. Existing planned structural fragments remain owned.

Empty edits immediately return the original vector. Validation errors occur before any input mutation or capacity change. Tests verify bytes, pointer and capacity recovery and that errors survive dropped data and edits.

Hardened planner operations that consume public scanner coordinates: checked template slicing and empty-series handling; validated consumed structural ranges; replaced template range-length debug assertions with typed errors; rejected overlapping template index/order ranges.

Integration tests compare owned output against borrowed output for all ChartEdit variants, exact/spare capacity, growth, shrinkage, Unicode labels, same-anchor series inserts/appends, adjacent spans, malformed coordinates, and late validation errors.
limitations: Validation covers this isolated chart component, not a full document engine or visual rendering workflow.
Allocation failure follows standard Vec behavior; allocation failure recovery is not introduced.
No benchmark or allocator instrumentation was run. Allocation reuse is checked through vector pointer and capacity assertions and the implementation avoids full-document duplicate buffers.
